senses.definition: present participle and gerund of stop
The act of something that stops; a halt.
(dentistry, dated) Material for filling a cavity in a tooth.

quotes.text: curious antiquaries, sifting the ruins of time, when London is a grass-grown path and all those hurrying along the pavement this Wednesday morning are but bones with a few wedding rings mixed up in their dust and the gold stoppings of innumerable decayed teeth
quotes.reference: 1925, Virginia Woolf, Mrs. Dalloway, Harcourt, Brace & World, Inc., page 23:

quotes.text: Then one day a big stopping came out of one of my back teeth.
quotes.reference: 1958, Henno Martin, translated by Edward Fitzgerald, The Sheltering Desert, New York: Thomas Nelson, page 125:

senses.definition: (mining) A partition or door to direct or prevent a current of air.
A pad or poultice of dung or other material applied to a horse's hoof to keep it moist.
examples:
1831-1850, William Youatt, On the Structure and the Diseases of the Horse
The drawing poultices and stoppings of farriers are often highly injurious, instead of abating inflammation .
